previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A homeless man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and hepatitis C was admitted for worsening right toe pain and swelling. An X-ray showed findings concerning for chronic osteomyelitis, but the podiatry team determined no surgical intervention was needed. He was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and clindamycin. His atrial fibrillation was rate-controlled, and rivaroxaban was safely restarted given resolved thrombocytopenia and absence of recent hemoptysis. Lisinopril was also restarted as prior hyponatremia had resolved. The patient was discharged home but left against medical advice before receiving full discharge paperwork. Follow-up was arranged with primary care and podiatry, with alerts placed to ensure continuity of care.
